What symptoms do citrus trees exhibit when affected by gummosis?

Gummosis in citrus trees presents a range of symptoms, including yellowing of leaves, cracking of bark, and profuse gumming on the surface. As the disease progresses, the bark may become rotten, resulting in tree drying due to a girdling effect. Affected trees often exhibit heavy blossoming, followed by premature death before fruit maturity. These symptoms collectively contribute to the characteristic appearance of foot rot or collar-rot in citrus orchards.
